 Learn more Image from Pixabay Today's big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks? 
 Micron Technology (MU) stock has lost 24.4% over the past month, against a 7.4% fall for the S&P 500. Yet the business is far more profitable than a year ago, with a net margin of 63.8% over its latest four quarters. That compares with 22.8% over the four quarters before. Management expects margins to expand over the rest of fiscal 2027 from the first quarter's level. It said that expansion would come from price increases that continue, but at a more moderate pace. So what happens to Micron if prices stop rising? Its profits would stay high, but its stock can still swing hard. In the 2022 inflation shock, it fell 49%. 
 Micron stock has lost 24.4% in just one month. If you are holding cash until it looks cheaper, that money does not have to sit idle while you wait. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays . 
 Micron Still Expects Prices To Rise, But More Slowly 
 On the September 30, 2026 call, management said it expects prices to keep rising at a lower rate into fiscal 2028. Start-up costs would partly offset the gains from prices and product mix. It also expects market conditions to stay tight through that year. 
 Near-term guidance reflects a similar outlook. Management guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $60 billion to $63 billion, following the $54.2 billion reported for fiscal Q4 2026. Executives said this guidance assumes only single-digit sequential growth in DRAM and NAND shipments. The company set a GAAP gross margin guide of 86.0% for fiscal Q1 2027, compared with the 86.8% gross margin reported in fiscal Q4 2026. Prices that stop rising would therefore be a worse outcome than management forecasts. 
 How Much Micron Would Earn If Prices Froze 
 Micron would earn $151 billion a year if its fiscal Q4 2026 net income simply repeated, a rough picture of flat prices. That is the latest quarter multiplied by four, not a forecast. Micron's market value is 5.2 times that figure . 
 Under this scenario, flat prices would still leave Micron very profitable. The larger risk for a holder is how hard the stock itself can swing. During the 2022 inflation shock, Micron stock fell 49%, compared with 24% for the S&P 500. 
 Micron Holds Far More Cash Than Debt 
 On September 3, 2026, Micron held $43.4 billion of cash and short-term investments against $5.18 billion of debt. Over its latest four quarters, the company also produced $59.0 billion of free cash flow after $30.7 billion of capital spending. 
 Story Continues This cash position would matter most if prices fell rather than simply stopped rising. In fiscal 2023, Micron's revenue fell 49.5% and the company lost $5.83 billion. Its free cash flow that year was negative $6.12 billion, meaning it spent more than it took in. At $38.3 billion, Micron's cash net of debt is about six times that shortfall. Even a repeat of that year would leave Micron with plenty of cash to spare. 
 What Micron's December Report Will Show 
 Micron is expected to release its next report in December 2026. The results will show the company's fiscal Q1 2027 gross margin against management's guide. 
 Even a business this profitable can see its stock swing hard. If Micron is a large share of your savings, it is worth planning how you would step out of it.
